problem: LiDAR-geometry-only mapless outdoor navigation (e.g. MTG) cannot distinguish geometrically similar but semantically different regions (crosswalk vs. road, flower bed, curbs, low grass). Image-only or VLM-only methods (ViNT, NoMaD, PIVOT with random candidates, CoNVOI) give non-traversable, non-smooth or unreliable trajectories.
motivation: Human-centered outdoor environments require contextual understanding (walk on sidewalks, cross at zebra crossings, go around buildings) that segmentation methods handle poorly without labeled data. VLMs offer zero-shot commonsense reasoning but cannot output precise spatial trajectories, though they can pick among visually annotated discrete options. So the paper pairs a geometry-based generator that guarantees traversable candidates with a VLM that picks the semantically best one.
key_idea: Generate diverse LiDAR-traversable candidate trajectories with a CVAE, overlay them as numbered lines on the RGB image, and let GPT-4V zero-shot pick the most human-like, socially compliant one.
insight: The generator's candidate quality is critical: replacing the CVAE with random linear candidates (PIVOT-style) or CoNVOI-style label-connected paths often leaves no viable option for the VLM, or yields paths crossing obstacles (Fig. 4, qualitative). The VLM selector matters: swapping it for the MTG shortest-distance heuristic cuts through buildings and misses humans, while the VLM goes around (Fig. 5, qualitative). Geometry supplies traversability and semantics supplies human-like choice; the ablations are qualitative only.
method: CVAE trajectory generator (MTG): an attention-based CVAE takes consecutive LiDAR frames and robot velocities, and the condition embedding is projected through linear transforms onto orthogonal axes to decode multiple diverse ~10m trajectories; trained with traversability loss, CVAE lower bound and diversity loss
Temporal redundancy: candidates from t=2 consecutive time steps are pooled into a set T to raise the chance that at least one is traversable
Hausdorff pruning: keeps a subset T' where pairwise Hausdorff distance exceeds a threshold dt, removing near-duplicates for clearer annotation and diversity
Visual marking module: projects trajectories to the image plane with the LiDAR-to-camera matrix K, draws lines, and numbers them by distance from the last waypoint to the goal (0 = closest)

VLM selector: GPT-4V receives the annotated image and a context prompt (wheeled robot, stay on pavement, avoid curbs and rough terrain, follow rules) and returns one trajectory number as JSON; re-prompted every 2-4 s
Execution: GPS gives goal direction; the selected trajectory is followed by a DWA local planner while awaiting the next VLM answer

setting.backbone: CVAE trajectory generator (trained) + GPT-4V (frozen, zero-shot selector)
setting.training_data: CVAE trained on the GND global navigation dataset (LiDAR point clouds, velocities, binary traversability maps, random targets with shortest ground-truth trajectories); VLM is training-free
setting.observation: 3D LiDAR (Velodyne VLP16) + monocular RGB (RealSense D435i) + robot velocities + GPS relative goal
setting.action_space: selected 10m local trajectory executed by DWA planner (continuous velocity)
setting.privileged: none at inference (binary traversability map is used only for training and evaluation)

numbers.extra: real-world Clearpath Husky data; own benchmark
own benchmark; CoNVOI has higher traversability (88.46)
single run per method; failures = human interventions; goal ~100m away behind a building
numbers.evidence: Table II Real World Experiment Results

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjNav benchmarks; results are on the authors' own outdoor scenarios. Ablations are qualitative (figures) only.
results: VL-TGS reaches the best traversability in 3 of 4 scenarios (87.22/89.93/87.44%; CoNVOI wins Corner with 88.46 vs 78.00) and the best Fréchet distance to human teleoperation in 3 of 4 (5.27/6.38/8.49 m; PIVOT is best on Curb at 7.86 vs 7.93), with average improvements of 20.81% traversability and 28.51% Fréchet distance. In a ~100m real-world run it had the fewest failures (4 vs 6 for NoMaD, 8 for MTG, 13 for CoNVOI) and the shortest distance and time.
limitations: Depends on GPT-4V robustness and its 2-4 s latency; long 10m trajectories and DWA mitigate this
Small evaluation: 20 frames per scenario and a single real-world run per method; ablations are qualitative only
Benchmark scenarios are mostly static and self-designed; GPS goal used; results depend on candidate quality from the CVAE
